title: Anurag Kashyap Opens Up About Age Gap With Shubhra Shetty, Emotional Bond
excerpt: The filmmaker, 53, revealed he once tried to push away his partner due to growing self-consciousness about their age difference, and teared up recalling a moment that made him 'want to live.'
body:
• Anurag Kashyap, 53, admitted he became increasingly self-conscious about the age gap with partner Shubhra Shetty, who is in her 30s, and once tried to push the relationship away.
  • Shubhra revealed she does not believe in marriage, while Kashyap said he is content with preserving what they have together.
  • The filmmaker teared up recalling an early moment in their relationship when Shubhra casually said she could "happily die now" after finding love, prompting him to realize he had found "something worth living for."
  • Kashyap was previously married to editor Aarti Bajaj (2003-2009) and actor Kalki Koechlin (2011-2015).

Filmmaker Anurag Kashyap has spoken candidly about his relationship with Shubhra Shetty, addressing the age difference between them and revealing an emotional turning point that deepened their bond. In an interview with journalist Janice Sequeira, the couple discussed love, marriage, and why Kashyap once tried to end things, according to Bollywood Hungama.

Kashyap, 53, and Shetty, who is in her 30s, have been together for several years. The director acknowledged that their age gap — which first drew public attention when their relationship became known around 2015 — has been a source of internal tension for him.

Self-Consciousness and the Decision to Push Away

"We've had our share of troubles. We've had our moments. We have been self-conscious," Kashyap said in the interview. Shetty quickly corrected him: "You have been more conscious."

Kashyap agreed, explaining how the dynamic shifted as he aged. "I was more conscious. And not just more conscious, at one point, I became so conscious, I was trying so hard to push it away," he said, per Bollywood Hungama. "Her face doesn't show her age. She still looks the same. She doesn't look her age. So the thing is, the more I grew older and she kept looking the same, that's when I became slightly conscious."

Shetty recalled that Kashyap had encouraged her to live independently and discover herself. "He was adamant that I go out, and if I have to find my way back to him, I will," she said.

The Moment That Changed Everything

The couple shared an emotional moment from the early stages of their relationship. Shetty recalled casually telling Kashyap that being in love was on her bucket list and that she could "happily die now."

"Before this, I was never scared if I got into a car accident. I just didn't care about anything. I feel like, for the first time in my life, I've found something worth living for, so I actually don't want to die."

— Anurag Kashyap, filmmaker

As Shetty recounted the memory during the interview, Kashyap became emotional and teared up again, according to Bollywood Hungama.

On Marriage and What Matters

When asked about the possibility of a third marriage, Kashyap revealed that Shetty does not believe in the institution. "She doesn't believe in it," he said. The filmmaker, who was previously married to editor Aarti Bajaj from 2003 to 2009 and actor Kalki Koechlin from 2011 to 2015, said his focus is on the relationship itself. "I'm very happy to be with her. I want to be with her. So, whatever that takes," he said.

Kashyap also reflected on how aging has shifted his priorities. "What is an old man's insecurity? I want to be healthy enough to outlive the people I love," he said. "As long as we have found what we have found now, I'm happy with anything. I don't want to lose this."

Looking Ahead

Kashyap remains one of Indian cinema's most prominent independent voices, with films like Gangs of Wasseypur, Dev D, and the Sacred Games series to his credit. Earlier this month, he reunited with filmmaker Imtiaz Ali to present the short film Bobby Beauty Parlour during Friendship Week. In July, he distanced himself from the Bobby Deol-starrer Bandar, saying "whatever came out is not my final cut." Shetty, who was an associate at Kashyap's former production house Phantom Films, continues to work in the industry.
